figures.caption: Figure 1: Causal diagram and the associated Single World Intervention Graph when intervening on the treatment, mediator and study indicator. A: treatment, Y : outcome, C: baseline confounders, M : mediator, S: study indicator. The arrow from S to A reflects differences in treatment assignment mechanisms across studies. Arrows from S to Y and M capture study-specific methodological differences affecting the outcome and mediator.
Figure 3: Treatment-Outcome heterogeneity across countries. Forest plot of the estimated effects for each country using TMLE and OS.
Figure 2: Treatment-Mediator heterogeneity across countries. Forest plot of the estimated effects for each country using TMLE and OS.
Table 4: Performance of the summary estimator ζ̂ across estimators under scenarios with and without missing data.

Table 3: Median ANOVA decomposition terms (η2, ξ2, and interaction) across 500 simulations, by estimator and nuisance model, under scenarios with and without missing data. The oracle values are computed from the true ζk,p values. RF denotes Random Forest-based nuisance estimation, and GLM denotes generalized linear models.
Table 1: Natural indirect effect (NIE) and proportion of treatment effect (PTE) estimands with their EIF. OR-PTE simplifies to the natural direct effect on the OR scale.

Table 2: Performance of estimators under outcome and mediator misspecification, under scenarios with and without missing data. RF denotes Random Forest-based nuisance estimation, and GLM denotes generalized linear models. Performances are averaged over the 25 estimators {ζ̂k,p}k,p. Var(ζ̂k,p) denotes the empirical variance over the Monte Carlo replications and V̂ar(ζ̂k,p) denotes the median of the estimated variances across simulations.
